findings.description: go_json_hash reapplies HTML and JavaScript string escaping. Production domain.Hash canonicalizes json.Marshal bytes via canonical.JSON and jsontext.Value.Canonicalize (JCS), whose strings use minimal representation.
findings.impact: Existing schema SQL contains > and <>. The Python schema hash differs from correct target_schema_sha256 even when schema is unchanged, making expected_state_matches false and preventing reliable independent positive-state validation.
findings.scenario: The illustrative string-only array [CHECK(epoch>0)] serializes with literal > under JCS but \u003e in this API; the two independently calculated digests differ. No target/native/SQL was executed.
findings.recommendation: Replace go_json_hash with a serializer restricted to its actual string/list/string-keyed-dict domain: reject invalid Unicode, order keys by UTF-16 code units, use minimal JSON string escaping with literal < > & U+2028/U+2029, no numeric support unless a full JCS number algorithm is implemented.

accepted_source_aspects: First 51 lines and eight bootstrap helpers are AST-identical to accepted v2 launch bootstrap.
Actions are explicit poll/snapshot/sign/publish/inspect/release/stop; approval construction is absent.
Signing/publication/release consume separately supplied exact approval refs and controller semantics.

Private issuer file is never read by API; its path is derived from exact pinned metadata, passed transiently to signer CLI, omitted from persisted public argv/results and cleared from local issuer variable.
Typed SQL row encoding matches production Go storage classes and big-endian lengths/float bits.
Read-only URI and query_only are used; reader module/DLL/DB guards close before inspection receipt publication.
Inspection completion booleans denote traversal, while expected_state_matches remains distinct and release remains a separate Root decision.
limitations: Only static source verified; no actual DB or signature operation.
Schema/type digest mismatch is an inspect blocker only; previously accepted v2 server launch is unchanged.
Caller-provided snapshot must be the separately reviewed concrete controller snapshot; inspection booleans do not grant Owner/native/formal authority.
No assertion that private path is absent from transient signer process arguments; claim is no persistent public receipt/log exposure.
